name: Ephraim (Joseph's son)
title: The younger who became greater
summary: Ephraim was the youngest son of Joseph and his Egyptian wife Asenath. Although he was younger than his brother Manasseh, he received the greater blessing from his grandfather Jacob. His descendants became one of the most powerful tribes in Israel and gave their name to the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Birth in Egypt
keyEvents.description: Ephraim was born in Egypt as Joseph's second son, before the seven years of famine began. Joseph named him Ephraim, which means 'fruitful', because God had made him fruitful in his land of affliction.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's blessing
keyEvents.description: When Jacob was old and weak, he blessed Joseph's sons. Jacob deliberately crossed his hands and placed his right hand on the younger Ephraim's head, giving him the greater blessing over Manasseh.

keyEvents.title: The Prophecy of Greatness
keyEvents.description: Jacob prophesied that Ephraim's descendants would become greater than Manasseh's and grow into a multitude of nations. This prophecy was fulfilled when the tribe of Ephraim became dominant in the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Adopted as Jacob's Son
keyEvents.description: Jacob declared that Ephraim and Manasseh should be counted as his own sons, on equal footing with Reuben and Simeon, and thus each receive a tribe in Israel.
